Subject: Monitoring integration playbook — Datadog / OTLP / Grafana dashboards

Hi Priya / Carlos / Lina —

Thanks again for taking the time last week. We kicked off an internal scoping meeting and sketched an initial partner ops playbook for shipping Redwood inference telemetry into leading monitoring stacks (Datadog, OTLP consumers, Grafana Cloud). I attached a short outline (redwood-otel-schema.md) and a sample Grafana dashboard JSON to this thread.

High-level goal: make it trivial for ops/SRE teams to get model-level observability (latency histograms, per-model QPS, error rates, per-request traces and request/response sizes) with minimal config changes. MVP scope we’re proposing:
- Metrics: per-model request_count, token_count, lat_p50/95/99, grpc/http error_count, tail_latency_bucketed
- Traces: span for request->model->cache + sampling to keep SaaS costs bounded
- Logs: structured request logs with customer_id/model_id/request_id; push to Loki or Datadog Logs
- Tags: customer_id, workspace, model_id, endpoint, region, backend_variant

Questions for you:
1) Datadog: recommended ingestion path — Datadog agent vs direct OTLP->Datadog OTLP endpoint? Any best practices for high-cardinality model tags?
2) Grafana: dashboard provisioning format you prefer for partner-distributed dashboards? Any limits/quirks for big cardinality metrics?
3) Security: what evidence do you need for SOC2/compliance review for a marketplace listing?

Suggested next step: 45m tech sync next week (proposal slots in Calendly: https://calendly.com/redwood/partner-onboard).

Thanks — happy to iterate on the MVP checklist before the call.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Monitoring integration playbook — Datadog / OTLP / Grafana dashboards

Jonas —

Great to hear from you and excited about this. Datadog has a couple of common patterns we recommend depending on volume:
- Low-to-medium volume: use OTLP -> Datadog OTLP endpoint (we host it) or run Datadog agent with an OTLP receiver.
- High volume: use Datadog agent as a forwarder with site-level aggregation and histogram aggregation on our side.

Notes/questions from our side:
* High-cardinality tags: model_id and customer_id are common, but recommend using a separate label for high-cardinality identifiers (e.g., model_shard or model_variant) and using Datadog's tag remapper to limit cardinality in billing-sensitive views.
* Traces: we can accept OTLP traces; please send a sample trace span schema.
* Logs: for ingress we prefer JSON structured logs. If you plan to send both traces and logs, let us know ingestion rates so we can advise cost optimization.

Security/compliance: we’ll need a short questionnaire and an architecture diagram showing where secrets/API keys live. SOC2 evidence we usually accept: network diagrams, encryption-at-rest/in-transit statements, and any pen-test reports.

I’ll loop in our solutions engineering lead if you want a hands-on walkthrough — copying Carlos to see overlap with Grafana dashboards.

Best,
Priya
Priya Rao

Subject: Re: Monitoring integration playbook — Datadog / OTLP / Grafana dashboards

Team —

Appreciate the context and the spec. A few notes from Grafana side: we recommend providing a dashboard JSON that uses templated variables for customer_id and model_id so teams can provision a single dashboard and use provisioning to bind it per-tenant. Grafana Cloud supports both Prometheus and OTLP metrics via Tempo/OTLP pipeline; for logs we recommend using Loki with labels that mirror your OTLP resource attributes (workspace/model_id).

A couple of practical items:
- Dashboard provisioning file format: grafana-sample-dashboard.json works fine; include the UID field and panel IDs to enable idempotent updates via provisioning.
- Cardinality: for very high-cardinality model_id tags, consider aggregating model_id into model_family on our dashboards for global views and keep model_id for per-tenant drilldowns.
- Demo: we can do a quick import demo of the sample dashboard during the sync; I can show how to set up provisioning via Grafana Cloud.

Regarding marketplace listing & security: we can accept the same compliance artefacts Datadog asked for; additionally, for Grafana Cloud integrations we ask for a short README that explains provisioning steps.

Looking forward to the call.

—Carlos
Integrations PM, Grafana Labs
carlos@grafana.com
